title: The hidden sources of spurious fusion transcripts in plants.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the GitHub repo tree and Zenodo record 19881401 (one 12 MB code zip). Downloaded examples/mh63_flagleaf.pc: 725 rows, no header, columns = partner gene IDs, breakpoint coordinates, confidence class (e.g. HC-b), strands, read counts, read ID, Inter/Intra flag; no artifact-vs-genuine label column. Repo contains rule-based breakpoint-classification scripts (SHS/Joined/Misaligned/Unknown).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Counts of 725 / 146 / 4,164 fusion calls (Iso-Seq, direct RNA, PCR-cDNA) in Table S2; artifact categories and validation results in Tables S5-S20. Europe PMC supplementary endpoint timed out, so the 22-tab Excel workbook was not opened. Raw reads in SRA PRJNA1291274 (not downloaded, raw sequencing).

a1_downloadable.note: Code and example outputs open on GitHub/Zenodo (MIT licence); supplementary Excel not retrieved (endpoint timeout).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked the example file: no genuine-vs-artifact column. The paper concludes almost all fusions are artifacts, so a 'genuine fusion' positive class essentially does not exist and would have to be constructed.

a3_inputs_present.note: Breakpoint coordinates and gene IDs present; sequences would need extraction from the MH63 genome (one reference, feasible).

a4_units_stated.note: Categorical calls and read counts; units not an issue.

a5_enough_rows.note: 725 Iso-Seq calls verified in example file; paper reports ~5,000 total across platforms (not verified).

a6_fits_laptop.note: Processed tables are small; raw reads not needed.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Example Iso-Seq file has 725 rows, matching the paper's 725 Iso-Seq fusions.

a8_label_provenance.note: The only available per-fusion labels (SHS / Joined / Misaligned / Unknown artifact type) come from a rule-based script applied to breakpoint sequences, so predicting them from sequence features would just re-learn the rule. Experimentally tested fusions are a handful of PCR validations.

honest_claim_h3: A model could at best reproduce the authors' rule-based artifact categories for rice fusion calls; it could not say whether any fusion is biologically real.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use sequence around the junction of a detected fused RNA read to predict whether it is a lab artifact or a real fusion.
plain_idea.train_on: Fusion calls from rice long-read RNA sequencing: partner genes, junction coordinates and read support; 725 Iso-Seq calls verified, ~5,000 across platforms per the paper.
plain_idea.predict: Artifact type (short-homology template switching, misalignment, etc.), but these labels come from the authors' own rule-based script, not an independent measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Plant genomics labs would get a filter for false fusion calls, but the paper's own rules already do this.

ml_idea: Classify detected fusion transcripts as artifact vs genuine from junction sequence; not viable because there are effectively no genuine positives and artifact labels are rule-derived.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; rejected at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count experimentally confirmed genuine fusions in Tables S2-S20: the paper implies near zero.

verdict_reason: Fails A2 and A8: no genuine-fusion positive class exists (paper concludes nearly all are artifacts), and the per-fusion artifact categories come from a rule-based script run on the same junction sequences a model would use, so it would just relearn the rule.
